# Galeed

**Galeed records what your LLM system did, step by step, separately from the
answer it gave.** Each request gets a trace of structured events (retrieval
ran, the planner chose X, the critic rejected Y), and each model call gets one
record holding its complete prompt and complete output. When an answer is
wrong, you can see why.

The core is pure Python stdlib, so any project can adopt it. Its companion
**[Mizpah](https://github.com/gellsmore-svg/Mizpah)** is the browser that
views what Galeed records. The names come from Genesis 31:48: one memorial
heap called *Galeed* ("heap of witness") and *Mizpah* ("watchtower"). Galeed
records; Mizpah views.

## Is it for you?

**Good fit:** you build multi-step or recursive LLM flows (agents, retrieval,
debate, pipelines) and need to replay exactly what each step saw and produced,
or stitch one trace across several services.

**Not a fit:** you want a hosted observability product, metrics dashboards, or
general application logging. Galeed stores traces in your own MongoDB and is
built for debugging LLM flows.

## Try it

```bash
pip install "galeed[cli]"          # core + the `galeed` CLI (adds rich, pymongo)
```

```python
from pymongo import MongoClient
from galeed import Tracer, EventType, capture_llm_call

db = MongoClient()["mnemosyne_dev"]          # the CLI's default database
t = Tracer(session_id="demo", source="my-app", db=db)

t.emit(EventType.PROCESS_STARTED, summary="answer a question")
with capture_llm_call(db, trace_id=t.trace_id, session_id="demo",
                      source="my-app", step_name="draft", prompt="Hi") as call:
    call.output = my_model("Hi")             # your model call
t.emit(EventType.PROCESS_COMPLETED)
```

```bash
galeed trace --session demo        # the In→Out call tree; --verbose for timings and metadata
```

Point anything at another store with `GALEED_MONGO_URI` / `GALEED_MONGO_DB`
(defaults: `mongodb://localhost:27017` / `mnemosyne_dev`).

## How it works

There are two layers, so traces stay light while full detail stays available:

- **Spine events** (`trace_events`) are small, ordered, typed records:
  `process.started`, a retrieval step, a decision. A `Tracer` is created once
  per request or operation and stamps every event with the trace, session and
  request ids.
- **LLM call records** (`llm_calls`) hold the heavy payloads: the complete
  prompt or messages, the complete output, a human `step_name`, usage and
  duration, and a `parent_call_id` so recursive flows form a tree.

**Tracing never breaks your application.** Persistence is best effort: a store
failure is swallowed and logged at DEBUG, and `db=None` keeps events in memory
only. Events also go to an in-process bus (`get_bus()`) for live streaming,
such as SSE to a process panel.

## What's in the box

| Module | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `events` | The event vocabulary (`EventType`, `TraceEvent`), extensible |
| `recorder` | `Tracer` plus query helpers over stored traces |
| `llm_calls` | `capture_llm_call(...)` / `record_llm_call(...)` for full model-call I/O |
| `bus` | Process-wide pub/sub (`TraceBus`) for live tails |
| `decisions` | Events recording *why* a run chose accept / reject / open |
| `feedback` | Lightweight feedback events tied to a trace |
| `cairn` | `emit_cairn_observation(...)`: events that [Huldah](https://github.com/gellsmore-svg/Huldah) can analyse as human-load and agent-effectiveness evidence |
| `hooks` | `galeed-codex-hook`, which streams a coding agent's lifecycle into the spine |

## Viewing traces

- `galeed trace`: call trees for every source. Filter with
  `--session/--trace/--source/--step/--call/--status/--since`, tail live with
  `--follow`, export with `--json` (which works without the `cli` extra).
- `galeed sessions` / `galeed events`: session summaries, including which
  calls lack usage or duration data, and raw events.
- `galeed serve` (`pip install "galeed[web]"`, port 8785): the HTTP trace API
  that browser viewers read. [Mizpah](https://github.com/gellsmore-svg/Mizpah)
  points here by default.

## Tracing a coding agent

`galeed-codex-hook` maps **Codex CLI** lifecycle hooks into Galeed events
(`source="codex"`). In `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```toml
[hooks]
SessionStart = ["galeed-codex-hook", "SessionStart"]
PreToolUse   = ["galeed-codex-hook", "PreToolUse"]
PostToolUse  = ["galeed-codex-hook", "PostToolUse"]
Stop         = ["galeed-codex-hook", "Stop"]
```

The handler reads the hook payload as JSON on stdin and uses the same
`GALEED_MONGO_*` variables. Other agents with command hooks can call it too,
but only the Codex payload shape is mapped today. Rollout plan:
[Noa codex-integration-plan](https://github.com/gellsmore-svg/Noa/blob/main/docs/codex-integration-plan.md).

## Joining traces across projects

Populate the standard `CORRELATION_KEYS` (`request_id`, `session_id`,
`trace_id`, `plan_id`, `job_id`). `galeed.correlation_ids(event)` reads them
back from fields and metadata, so one trace can be stitched across services.
Hoglah, Tirzah, Mahalath, Deborah, Huldah and Milcah all emit into the same
spine this way.

Events carry `schema_version` (`galeed.SCHEMA_VERSION`). It is bumped only for
a backwards-incompatible change to the event shape; new event types are
additive.

## Develop

Stdlib-only, so it behaves the same on Linux and WSL.

```bash
pip install -e ".[dev]"
pytest
```

# Security

## Reporting

Report vulnerabilities via GitHub issues (or privately to the repository owner
for sensitive reports). This is a local-first family project; there is no bug
bounty.

## Data sensitivity: `llm_calls` stores complete prompts and outputs

The LLM debugging layer is **full-fidelity by design**: every captured call's
COMPLETE prompt/messages and COMPLETE output are persisted to the `llm_calls`
collection. Anything a tool puts into a prompt — retrieved memory, user
questions, session history, document excerpts — ends up readable there.

Operational guidance:

- Treat the trace database (`mnemosyne_dev` by default) with the same
  sensitivity as the source data it summarises.
- `galeed serve` is **read-only but unauthenticated**; it binds `127.0.0.1`
  by default and must not be exposed beyond localhost without an
  authenticating proxy.
- Capture is opt-in per emitter (e.g. Hoglah's `galeed_capture_io`), and can be
  disabled while keeping lean lifecycle events.
- To purge captured payloads: drop or TTL-index the `llm_calls` collection —
  spine events are unaffected (they carry no payloads).

## Emission safety

Emission is best-effort by contract: persistence or bus failures are swallowed
(optionally visible at `DEBUG` log level) and must never affect the emitting
pipeline.

# Galeed — functional and code review

**Date:** 2026-08-08 · **Reviewed:** `master` @ `35a226f`, `pyproject` at
**0.3.2** (four files uncommitted: `decisions.py`, its test, CHANGELOG, version)
**Method:** the CLI and HTTP API were exercised against the **live
`mnemosyne_dev` spine** (235 `llm_calls`, 2,300+ trace events, read-only), the
cost helpers and hook bridge were probed directly, then the source was read.
Every claim below is backed by a run or a query, reproduced inline.

> **Disclosure.** The token-usage/cost work in `src/galeed/llm_calls.py`
> (commit `77a5bc4`) was written by this reviewer. Two findings — H1 and M3 —
> are against that code, and H3 is against a claim this reviewer made elsewhere.

---

## Part 1 — Functional review

**Baseline:** `46 passed` in 0.71 s. `ruff check src tests` clean, rule set
pinned with the explanatory comment, CI gates both. Stdlib-only core, as
advertised.

### What works

**`galeed trace` delivers exactly what the README promises.** Run against the
live spine it renders the full In→Out call tree with the complete prompt
captured — not a truncated preview:

```
╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ 064471db-…  exp1-074844-4 · 1 call(s)                                        │
│ └── ● mistral-small:latest                                                   │
│     In:                                                                      │
│     Analyse the REASONING below for logical fallacies. Judge ONLY the form   │
│     of the inference …                                                       │
```

This is the debugging layer working as designed, and it is the reason the other
reviews in this estate could inspect what models were actually sent.

Also verified:

- `galeed sessions` summarises across sources (`codex`, `hoglah`, `tirzah`,
  `feedback`) with event and trace counts.
- The HTTP API answers `200` on `/api/trace/sessions`, `/api/llm-calls`, and
  `/api/trace/events`; binds `127.0.0.1`; read-only; the docstring says plainly
  there is no auth.
- `correlation_ids` handles every case correctly — flat fields, nested
  `metadata`, top-level winning over metadata on conflict, and non-string
  coercion.
- `TraceBus` uses bounded queues (`max_queue=1000`) with non-blocking
  `put_nowait` and drops on a slow consumer rather than blocking a request. That
  is the right trade for telemetry.
- `web.py` closes its `MongoClient` on shutdown **only when it opened it**
  (`owned_client`) — a careful version of a fix that is usually done bluntly.

### Functional defects

#### F1. The cost estimator cannot produce a non-zero number

`estimate_cost_usd` is the family's only cost function. Its rate table ships
with a single entry:

```python
DEFAULT_COST_PER_1M = {'default': {'in': 0.0, 'out': 0.0}}
```

There are no model rates at all, so every model resolves to the zero default:

```
cost(1M in + 1M out, model=None                 ) = 0.0
cost(1M in + 1M out, model=gemma4:e2b           ) = 0.0
cost(1M in + 1M out, model=claude-opus-5        ) = 0.0
cost(1M in + 1M out, model=gpt-5                ) = 0.0
```

Two million tokens on a frontier model costs `$0.00`, and that value is
indistinguishable from genuinely free local inference. The docstring is careful
about the *other* unknown — *"Returns `None` when usage has no token counts
(unknown, not free)"* — but an **unpriced model** silently becomes free rather
than unknown.

#### F2. Half the spine carries no cost or latency signal

Measured across all 235 live `llm_calls`:

```
usage.total > 0 :  91 (39%)      duration_ms set :  98 (42%)

  hoglah   n=116  usage>0= 91  duration= 98
  tirzah   n=119  usage>0=  0  duration=  0
```

The Hoglah instrumentation works. **Tirzah writes 119 calls with neither token
counts nor duration** — every direct answer-adapter call is uninstrumented.

This matters beyond Galeed. An earlier assessment in this estate asserted that
"104 LLM calls are recorded and zero carry duration or tokens" and treated
instrumenting them as the precondition for evaluating the architecture. That fix
was applied to Hoglah only. On today's data the estate still cannot answer what a
run costs, because the larger producer reports nothing and the estimator (F1)
could only return zero anyway.

Galeed is the spine and has no coverage reporting of its own — `galeed sessions`
shows event counts, never instrumentation coverage.

#### F3. The agent hooks add ~2 s per invocation when Mongo is unreachable

`_get_db()` opens a client with `serverSelectionTimeoutMS=2000` and issues
`client.admin.command("ping")` on **every** hook invocation. Measured against an
unroutable host:

```
_get_db() with Mongo unreachable: 2.12s, 2.01s
PreToolUse + PostToolUse per tool call => ~4.2s added per tool call
over 100 tool calls => ~7.1 minutes of added latency
```

The docstring says *"hooks must be best-effort and never block the agent."* It
never *fails* the agent, but two seconds per hook — twice per tool call, on every
tool call — is blocking in any practical sense. Each hook is a fresh process, so
nothing learns that Mongo is down and every invocation pays it again.

---

## Part 2 — Code review

### High

#### H1 · `llm_calls.py:91-113` — `estimate_cost_usd` conflates "unpriced" with "free"

```python
table = rates or DEFAULT_COST_PER_1M
rate = table.get(model or "", table.get("default", {"in": 0.0, "out": 0.0}))
```

Code side of F1. The function is structurally correct — it takes an injectable
`rates` table, normalises the token aliases, and returns `None` when usage
carries no counts. What is missing is that the shipped table has no rows, so the
`default` branch is the only branch ever taken.

**Fix:** return `None` when the model is not in the table and the caller supplied
no rates, reserving `0.0` for models explicitly priced at zero (local Ollama).
Optionally ship rates for the models the family actually calls. The one-line
version is:

```python
rate = table.get(model or "")
if rate is None:
    return None if model else table.get("default")
```

*(Reviewer's own code.)*

#### H2 · `hooks.py:38-51` — a 2 s connection probe on every hook invocation

```python
client = MongoClient(uri, serverSelectionTimeoutMS=2000)
client.admin.command("ping")   # quick check
```

Code side of F3. The `ping` is what makes the failure slow: without it, pymongo's
lazy connection would fail on the first write and could be given a much shorter
budget.

**Fix, cheapest first:** drop `serverSelectionTimeoutMS` to ~250 ms for the hook
path (a local Mongo answers in single-digit ms); and write a short-lived
breadcrumb (e.g. `~/.galeed/mongo-unreachable`, valid 60 s) so subsequent hook
processes skip the probe entirely rather than each re-paying it.

#### H3 · No instrumentation-coverage surface

Code side of F2. `record_llm_call` accepts a call with no `usage`, no
`duration_ms` and no `started_at` without comment — correctly, since telemetry
must never fail a request. But nothing anywhere reports how much of the spine is
instrumented, so a producer that silently stops reporting usage (as Tirzah never
started) is invisible.

Hanani solves exactly this problem with a first-class `gaps` command that states
its own coverage in plain language. The same idea belongs here: `galeed sessions`
should show, per source, what fraction of calls carry usage and duration. It is a
single aggregation over a collection Galeed already owns, and it is the cheapest
way to stop cost claims across the estate from drifting from the data.

### Medium

#### M1 · `events.py:24` — `SCHEMA_VERSION` is written and never read

```
src/galeed/events.py:24   SCHEMA_VERSION = "1.0"
src/galeed/events.py:154  schema_version: str = SCHEMA_VERSION
```

Those, plus the re-export in `__init__.py`, are the only occurrences. No reader —
not the CLI, not the web API, not the recorder — compares an event's
`schema_version` against the one it understands.

The README's schema discipline (*"bump it only on a backwards-incompatible
change"*) is therefore one-directional: producers stamp, consumers ignore. If the
version were bumped tomorrow, nothing would notice, which removes the only
benefit of carrying the field. Keturah, by contrast, validates
`MANIFEST_SCHEMA_VERSION` on read.

**Fix:** have the read paths warn (not fail) on an unrecognised major version.

#### M2 · `bus.py:36-40` — dropped events are silent

```python
try:
    sub.put_nowait(event)
except queue.Full:
    pass  # slow consumer: drop rather than block the request
```

Dropping is the right behaviour; doing it invisibly is not, in a component named
"heap of witness". A slow SSE viewer loses events and neither the publisher nor
the subscriber learns that the stream has holes.

**Fix:** a per-bus dropped counter, exposed on the bus and in `galeed sessions`.

#### M3 · `llm_calls.py:74-82` — alias normalisation stores each count twice

`_merge_usage` writes both spellings (`tokens_in` **and** `prompt_tokens`,
`tokens_out` **and** `completion_tokens`), so a stored `usage` holds five keys
for three numbers. Good for query compatibility, but any consumer that sums the
numeric values of `usage` — a natural thing to do with a token dict — double
counts. Live example:

```json
{"prompt_tokens": 4, "completion_tokens": 25, "total": 29}
```

(older record, pre-alias) versus a current one carrying all five. Consumers now
have to know which keys are canonical.

**Fix:** store the canonical pair plus `total`, and normalise aliases on read
instead. Failing that, document the canonical set in the README.
*(Reviewer's own code.)*

#### M4 · `cli.py:50` and `hooks.py:47` — `MongoClient` is never closed

Both are short-lived processes so nothing leaks in practice, and `web.py` — the
long-lived one — does close correctly. Recorded for completeness, and because the
hook path pays full connection setup per event (H2).

### Low

#### L1 · Uncommitted work in the tree

`decisions.py`, `tests/test_decisions.py`, `CHANGELOG.md` and the version bump to
0.3.2 are modified but not committed. The last release commit is 0.3.1. A fresh
clone gets neither.

---

## Comparison with the other six reviews

Galeed is the spine the other six emit into, which makes one finding here
disproportionately important: **F1 + F2 mean the estate's cost story is still not
answerable.**

That is worth stating plainly because this reviewer previously asserted the
opposite direction. The roles assessment identified "no cost instrument exists in
this stack" as the blocking gap and instrumenting it as action #1. The
instrumentation landed for Hoglah (78% usage coverage, verified above) and the
conclusion was treated as settled. On today's data:

- Tirzah — the larger producer, 119 of 235 calls — reports nothing at all;
- the cost estimator can only ever return `0.0` or `None`.

So the measurement that was supposed to make the architecture evaluable is half
wired and terminates in a constant. This is the estate's **degenerate-constant**
family (Hoglah's Prometheus counters, Milcah's `global_coherence`, Hanani's
all-`True` audit scores) appearing in the reviewer's own contribution, which is a
useful check on the pattern being real rather than a stylistic complaint.

The other estate-wide property holds here too, in its mildest and most
appropriate form: **silence**. A dropped bus event, an unstamped schema version,
an uninstrumented producer, a 2-second hook stall — all correct decisions for
telemetry taken individually (never fail the request), and all invisible
collectively. Galeed is the one product where "never fail, never mention" is
defensible by design; it is also the one where a coverage surface would pay for
itself across six consumers.

---

## Suggested order

1. **H1** — make unpriced models return `None`, not `0.0`. Five lines, and it
   stops a fabricated number entering every cost aggregate.
2. **H3** — per-source usage/duration coverage in `galeed sessions`. One
   aggregation; it is what would have caught F2 without a manual query, and the
   Hanani `gaps` command is the model to copy.
3. **F2 (Tirzah side)** — thread usage and duration through Tirzah's direct
   answer path, as Hoglah already does. Belongs in Tirzah's backlog, referenced
   here because Galeed is where the gap is visible.
4. **H2** — shorter hook timeout plus an unreachable breadcrumb.
5. **M1, M2** — schema-version warning on read, dropped-event counter.
6. **M3, M4, L1** — small.

Nothing here is architectural. The event vocabulary, the tracer, the bounded bus,
the ownership-aware client close and the In→Out debug view are all right, and the
trace viewer is the most useful single tool in the estate. The findings are one
empty lookup table, one missing aggregation, and one timeout.

# The trace spine

Every family project emits structured events into one stream (the
`trace_events` collection plus a live in-process bus). The vocabulary
(`EventType`) is **documented but open**: emitters may add types without a
schema bump; `SCHEMA_VERSION` changes only on a backwards-incompatible shape
change.

The documented sets: request lifecycle (`process.*`, `message.*`,
`answer.finalized`), retrieval/model steps, background jobs (`job.*` — Hoglah),
the Mahalath ontology pipeline (`document.ingested`, `debate.completed`,
`proposal.*`), Milcah coherence runs (`orchestration.*`, `snapshot.saved`),
plan interpretation (`plan.step.*`, emitted live by Tirzah's executor), and
`llm.call.completed/failed`.

**Correlation**: populate `CORRELATION_KEYS` (`request_id`, `session_id`,
`trace_id`, `plan_id`, `job_id` — the last two ride in metadata) so a flow can
be stitched across repos; `correlation_ids(event)` reads them back.

**Emission is best-effort by contract**: `Tracer.emit` and `record_event`
swallow persistence failures. A tool must behave identically with the spine
up, down, or absent.

# LLM debugging

Debugging an LLM system means seeing **exactly what context went into each
call and what text came out**. That material is deliberately kept OUT of spine
events (session listings must stay light), so it has its own home: the
`llm_calls` collection — one document per call with the COMPLETE `prompt` or
`messages` list, the COMPLETE `output` (or `error`), a human `step_name`, the
correlation ids, and `parent_call_id` so recursive/chained flows form a tree
(`call_tree`). Technical detail (model, timing, usage) rides in `metadata`,
which viewers reveal only in an advanced mode — the default view is pure
In→Out.

Emitters: **Hoglah records every generate job automatically** (call_id =
job_id; thread `metadata.trace_id` through a multi-step flow to join it into
one trace); **Tirzah** records every answer-adapter call; any other tool wraps
a direct call in `capture_llm_call(...)` or records after the fact with
`record_llm_call(...)`.

Viewers: `galeed trace` (CLI tree), `galeed serve` + **Mizpah's LLM Calls tab**
(browser).

# Galeed

Galeed ("heap of witness", Gen 31:48) is the family's shared logging capability:
a structured event stream separating **process telemetry** from the **final
answer**, plus the **LLM debugging layer** — one full In→Out document per model
call. Galeed *records*; Mizpah (the "watchtower") *views*.

## Map

- **[Concepts](concepts/index.md)** — the spine's design rules and the LLM
  debugging model.
- **[Modules](modules/index.md)** — events, recorder/bus, llm_calls, feedback,
  and the CLI/web viewers.

- **events** — the documented, extensible event vocabulary (`EventType`,
  `TraceEvent`, `SCHEMA_VERSION`, `CORRELATION_KEYS`).
- **recorder** — `Tracer` (per-request emitter: persist + bus) and the query
  helpers (`list_trace_events`, `list_trace_sessions`).
- **bus** — in-process pub/sub for live streaming (SSE process panels).
- **llm_calls** — full-fidelity call capture (`record_llm_call`,
  `capture_llm_call`, `list_llm_calls`, `call_tree`); payloads live here, spine
  events link by `call_id`.
- **cli** — `galeed trace | sessions | events | serve` (extras: `cli`, `web`).
- **web** — `galeed serve`, the read-only trace API browser viewers consume.

## Emitters

Hoglah (jobs, automatic), Tirzah (answer path + request traces), Mahalath
(ontology pipeline), Milcah (coherence runs) — all opt-in via config/env flags,
all best-effort: emission never raises into a pipeline.

# cairn

`emit_cairn_observation(...)` records a normal Galeed trace event with metadata
that Cairn can consume as live-observation evidence.

It keeps Galeed dependency-free and does not import Cairn. The bridge only
standardises the producer-side metadata:

- `cairn_kind`
- `tags`
- `human_systems`
- `duration_ms`
- `missing_evidence` when the tag is present
- `sufficient = false` when `missing_context` is present

Supported observation kinds are `ui_event`, `system_log`, `agent_step`,
`agent_output`, `agent_output_review`, `queue_event`, `feedback`, and
`recovery_event`.

# cli & web

**CLI** (`pip install galeed[cli]` → rich + pymongo):

- `galeed trace` — the debug view: In→Out per call, chains as trees,
  `--verbose` for the technical layer, filters
  (`--session/--trace/--source/--step/--call/--status/--since/--limit`),
  `--follow` (store-polling live tail), `--json` export (works core-only).
- `galeed sessions` / `galeed events` — spine rollups and raw events.
- Connection: `--mongo-uri/--mongo-db` or `GALEED_MONGO_URI`/`GALEED_MONGO_DB`
  (defaults: `mongodb://localhost:27017` / `mnemosyne_dev`).

**Web** (`pip install galeed[web]`): `galeed serve` (default `127.0.0.1:8785`)
— read-only FastAPI over the family Mongo: `/api/trace/sessions`,
`/api/trace/events`, `/api/trace/stream` (poll-based SSE, works across
processes), `/api/llm-calls[?payloads=false]`, `/api/llm-calls/{call_id}`,
`/api/health`. The `/api/trace/*` shapes match Tirzah's, so Mizpah works
against either; the llm-calls endpoints are what its LLM Calls tab reads.

# events

`TraceEvent` is the wire shape: trace/session ids, `type`, `status`, `summary`,
`severity`, `source`, optional message/request ids, `seq`, timestamp, and a
free `metadata` dict. `to_dict()` is the JSON-safe form used for storage, API
responses, and SSE frames.

`EventType` documents the family vocabulary (see the
[spine concept](../concepts/event-spine.md)); `KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES` derives from
it and is asserted by Tirzah's seam contract for its own emissions — the
vocabulary itself stays open. Id constructors (`new_trace_id`,
`new_message_id`, `new_request_id`, `new_event_id`) give collision-safe
prefixed uuids.

# llm_calls

One document per model call in the `llm_calls` collection (see the
[debugging concept](../concepts/llm-debugging.md)).

- `record_llm_call(db, trace_id=…, session_id=…, source=…, prompt=…/messages=…,
  output=…/error=…, step_name=…, parent_call_id=…, metadata=…)` — one-shot
  record after a call finishes; also mirrors a lean `llm.call.completed/failed`
  spine event unless `emit_event=False` (emitters whose lifecycle events
  already mark the spine, e.g. Hoglah's `job.*`, pass False).
- `capture_llm_call(db, …) as call:` — context-manager wrapper for direct
  calls: set `call.output` (and optionally `call.model`/`call.metadata`);
  an exception records the call as failed and re-raises.
- `list_llm_calls(...)` — filters (trace/session/source/step/status/call_id/
  since), oldest→newest; `include_payloads=False` returns lean rows with size
  counts. `get_llm_call`, `call_tree` (parent/child forest), `new_call_id`.

Everything is best-effort: a broken db yields empty results / silent skips,
never an exception into the caller.

# recorder & bus

`Tracer` is created once per request/operation (`trace_id` often anchored on an
existing run/job id). Each `emit()` builds a `TraceEvent`, appends it to
`tracer.events` (so a request can return its `processEvents` directly),
persists it best-effort to `trace_events`, and publishes it to the bus —
never raising into the caller. Convenience wrappers: `started` / `completed`
/ `failed`.

Query helpers: `list_trace_events(db, trace_id=…, session_id=…)` (replay for
dev-log windows) and `list_trace_sessions(db)` (per-session rollups: sources,
counts, first query, last answer preview).

`TraceBus` (`get_bus()`) is in-process pub/sub keyed by trace/session/`*` —
what powers live SSE process panels. Cross-process live tails poll the store
instead (`galeed serve`'s SSE endpoint, `galeed trace --follow`).

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=68", "wheel"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "galeed"
version = "0.4.1"
description = "Galeed — the cross-project trace/log spine: a structured event stream separating process telemetry from final output."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
license = {file = "LICENSE"}
authors = [
    {name = "gellsmore-svg"},
]
keywords = [
    "logging",
    "tracing",
    "observability",
    "event-stream",
    "telemetry",
    "local-first",
]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 3 - Alpha",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries :: Application Frameworks",
    "Topic :: System :: Logging",
    "Typing :: Typed",
]
# Intentionally dependency-free: the spine is pure stdlib so any project can adopt it.
dependencies = []

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/gellsmore-svg/galeed"
Repository = "https://github.com/gellsmore-svg/galeed"
Issues = "https://github.com/gellsmore-svg/galeed/issues"

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = ["pytest>=8"]
# The `galeed` debugging CLI (trace/sessions/events): pretty trees need rich,
# the store lives in the family MongoDB. `--json` output works core-only.
cli = ["rich>=13", "pymongo>=4.6"]
# `galeed serve` — the HTTP trace API browser viewers (Mizpah) read.
web = ["fastapi>=0.110", "uvicorn>=0.29", "pymongo>=4.6"]

[project.scripts]
galeed = "galeed.cli:main"
galeed-codex-hook = "galeed.hooks:main"

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["src"]

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
galeed = ["py.typed"]

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py311"

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Pin the rule set explicitly rather than inheriting ruff's defaults: ruff 0.16
# widened those defaults, which silently turns a green gate red on a tool
# upgrade. This is the historical default set (pyflakes + the pycodestyle
# errors worth gating), so the gate means the same thing on every ruff version.
select = ["E4", "E7", "E9", "F"]
